requirement:
A tracked read of an HC GitHub issue node records its identity and a fingerprint
of the supplied title, opening post, and status under
{cite}`requirements.sdk.graph.evidence.node_inputs`.
Changing any of those supplied fields changes the fingerprint under the same
fingerprinting rules. The fingerprint excludes cache fetch time and TTL;
refetching otherwise unchanged issue contents does not change it.

The fingerprint describes the issue contents supplied under HC's
[redaction policy](../authoring.md#habeas-req-requirements.authoring.redaction),
including the text presented to an agent.
rationale:
`requirements.sdk.habeas.github_nodes.inputs` has no tests. It has no `{test}` references or `:test:` anchors, and the outgoing `Tests` edges are empty. A text search for the requirement name finds only evidence files, with no test source.

**Obligations that need tests**
- A tracked read of a GitHub issue node records the node identity and a fingerprint of the supplied title, opening post, and status.
- Changing any one of title, opening post, or status changes the fingerprint.
- The fingerprint excludes cache fetch time and TTL, so refetching unchanged contents leaves it unchanged.
- The fingerprint covers the contents supplied under the redaction policy, including the text presented to an agent.

None of these is exercised or asserted anywhere.

The cited requirement `requirements.sdk.graph.evidence.node_inputs` is context only. I did not reassess its implementation or tests.

**Acknowledgment**
`src/sdk.rs#enum[HabeasNode]` carries a `{fixme}` on `requirements.sdk.habeas.github_nodes.inputs`. It names `nikomatsakis/habeas-codicem#26`, which is open. Its body says that tests do not yet cover the redacted contents, the field-sensitive fingerprints, or the fetch-time/TTL independence. That describes the same missing-test gap.

The enum has no GitHub issue variant, which matches the deferral the `{fixme}` describes. The only gap is the missing tests, and it is acknowledged.

Finishing a verification includes every successful tracked node read in its
`Fingerprinted`, whether ordinary code or a model tool requested it. Each observation
contains the node identity and the fingerprint of the contents actually supplied.
A failed read returns an error without inventing a successful observation.
Repeating an identical observation adds no information. Reading the same
identity with two different fingerprints preserves both observations.
